PullRequest.Title: test: put back the page scroll position after every top-level unit test suite
PullRequest.Body:
Restores the page scroll position after every top-level unit test suite, in both the browser and Electron unit runners. The warn-only scroll detector added in #345862 still reports the suite that scrolled the page.

**Why:** each runner, or each `--workers` process, runs many test files in one page. 14 test files leave that page scrolled, mostly to (0, 60), by focusing an input they appended below the fold. Every later suite that measures page coordinates then runs against a moved origin, so whether a layout test passes depends on which files its worker ran first. Over the last 48 h of PR CI, this failed PRs that don't touch these tests:
- `TabbedModelPicker › comparison preserves the normal list viewport and stays anchored after reopening` (`aligned: false`) on Linux and Windows Browser-Unit, in 2 unrelated PRs.
- `Artifact Integration Presentation` (`overlaps` and `aligned` flipped) on Windows Browser-Unit. That's the same test #345859 fixed last week for one polluter.

Fixing polluters one at a time doesn't stop new ones from appearing, so this resets the scroll at suite boundaries. `IIsolationDetector` gets an optional `reset(before)`. `installIsolationCheck` calls it after each detector's check in the existing top-level `afterAll`, and only `scrollDetector` implements it. The cost is a few property writes per suite.

**Evidence (local Chromium):**
- The scroll detector over the full browser unit suite (`--workers 4`) names the 14 files that scroll the page, for example `sessionGridLayout`, `sessionView`, `aiCustomizationListWidget`, `contentPart`, `extensionsViewlet` and `bannerPart`.
- I replayed the exact file list of the failing CI worker (462 files, then `modelPickerTabbedWidget`) with `--runList`, and the 2 TabbedModelPicker failures reproduce. Bisecting points to `sessionGridLayout.test.ts`, which leaves the page at (0, 60), and the test passes alone.
- **With this change:** the same 463-file list has 0 failures. The full suite with `--workers 4` loses the order-dependent failures (TabbedModelPicker and Artifact Integration Presentation). The remaining ChatOutline and Extensions viewlet failures in my local run also fail when run alone on `main` in my environment, so they're unrelated.
- `isolationCheck.test.ts` gets a test for the reset. It passes in Chromium (14) and Electron (15). eslint is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` shows no errors in these files.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser unit-test worker completes a top-level suite and advances to the next suite in the shared page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing afterAll isolation check reads scroll state, then the added reset synchronously assigns body/document scroll offsets and calls window.scrollTo before Mocha can advance. No geometry read follows the writes, so style/layout is not synchronously forced; rendering and scroll notification can be coalesced by the browser.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Five DOM/window scroll-state assignments across the browser/compositor boundary
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reset invocation per top-level suite; five constant property writes, with an actual scroll-state change only when the suite changed one of the captured positions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The detector only read and compared the three scroll representations; it did not restore them
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously at suite teardown, but does not perform a post-write layout read or wait for paint; only the property-call overhead is on the next-suite critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally append accumulated isolation findings to the report file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one append per browser run when VSCODE_TEST_ISOLATION_REPORT is enabled and findings exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single end-of-run append already reported detector findings
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the test run while emitting the optional report, not after each suite; normal successful resets do not add findings

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of top-level suites assigned to one worker; realistic full runs contain hundreds of files split across up to four workers. Cost is a fixed five assignments per suite, while meaningful scroll changes are limited to suites that moved the page.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Top-level suites are serialized within each browser page. CI may run up to four independent worker processes, each with its own browser/page, so there is no shared-page concurrency or burst within a worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or network lookup is involved. The existing per-suite snapshot is retained in a WeakMap and deleted at teardown; the diff does not alter its lifecycle or introduce retained keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous per-suite writes and serialized runner path from the changed reset through installIsolationCheck and the browser runner integration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser cost of assigning unchanged scroll values varies by engine, but the code has no forced-layout read, unbounded work, or per-element traversal, and browser rendering can coalesce the writes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added constant teardown work is bounded and does not establish a realistic latency, rendering, CPU, or memory regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron unit-test renderer completes a top-level suite and advances within the shared renderer page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same added scroll reset executes in the existing Mocha afterAll hook before the next top-level suite. It is synchronous but performs only fixed scroll writes after the detector's reads, without a read-after-write layout flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Five body/document/window scroll-state assignments in the Electron renderer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed-size reset per top-level suite in each worker; only suites that actually scrolled require a compositor-visible change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Suite teardown checked the captured scroll positions but left them unchanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The assignments execute before the next suite, but no paint, frame, IPC, or layout result is awaited

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously append optional isolation findings at the end of the run
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one append per renderer run when reporting is enabled and findings exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The optional end-of-run append already existed with the same cardinality
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: End-of-run reporting only; not moved into per-suite teardown by this diff

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Top-level suites run by one Electron worker, commonly hundreds distributed across up to four processes. Added work remains O(suites) with a small constant and O(1) memory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Suites are serialized in each Electron renderer. Worker mode uses separate Electron processes/windows (up to four in CI), so resets do not contend on one document.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted. Existing snapshots are removed after each suite, and reset retains no new objects beyond the current hook invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the Electron runner installation, sequential Mocha hook execution, and the changed detector implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Engine-specific scroll setter overhead is not measured, but there is no evidence of synchronous layout, IPC, filesystem access, retained state, or collection-sized work in the added path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The bounded property writes do not meet the evidence threshold for material test-run latency or resource pressure.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the full two-file diff and traced the added reset through browser and Electron test runners. Considered synchronous UI work and repeated per-suite work, including worker concurrency and optional report I/O. The diff adds only fixed scroll writes with no forced-layout read, external boundary fan-out, cache change, or retention; no performance finding or regression-fix record is warranted.
